title: Repair a missing field
prompt: Define get_label(row) using try/except KeyError. Return row["derived"] when present and "UNKNOWN" otherwise. Example: get_label({}) == "UNKNOWN".
tests:
assert get_label({}) == "UNKNOWN", "missing derived should be UNKNOWN"
assert get_label({"derived":"DRAW"}) == "DRAW", "preserve a present label"
hint: Place only the dictionary lookup inside try.

title: Repair a type mismatch
prompt: Define plays(text) to convert a numeric string to an integer and add one. Example: plays("6") == 7. Invalid numeric text returns None.
tests:
assert plays("6") == 7, "six recorded plays plus one should be seven"
assert plays("0") == 1, "zero plus one should be one"
assert plays("unknown") is None, "invalid text must remain unavailable"
hint: int(text) converts numeric text; conversion can raise ValueError.

title: Assert an elixir assumption
prompt: Define spend(elixir, cost). Assert 0 <= elixir <= 10, cost >= 0, and cost <= elixir, each with a clear message. Then return elixir - cost. Example: spend(10, 6) == 4.
hint: Write three assertions before the subtraction. These are learning checks, not a production input-validation design.
solution:
def spend(elixir, cost):
    assert 0 <= elixir <= 10, "elixir must be between 0 and 10"
    assert cost >= 0, "cost cannot be negative"
    assert cost <= elixir, "cost exceeds available elixir"
    return elixir - cost
